chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, who said: Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣahbān narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, who said: A number of our companions agreed upon this hadith. Among them were Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام; Ṣabbāḥ al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام; and Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام.

Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about this hadith, and he informed me of it, and said: All of these together asked us about the salat (prayer) in the month of Ramadan—how it is, and how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم acted.

They all said: When the first night of the month of Ramadan entered, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed the Maghrib salat (prayer), then he performed four rakʿahs which he used to perform after Maghrib every night, then he performed eight rakʿahs. Then when he had performed the ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah and the two rakʿahs which he used to perform after the ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah while seated every night, he stood and performed twelve rakʿahs, then entered his house. When the people saw that and observed that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم had increased in prayer when the month of Ramadan entered, they asked him about that. He informed them: I performed this salat because of the excellence of the month of Ramadan over the months. Then, when it was night, he stood to perform salat, and the people formed rows behind him. So he turned toward them and said: O people, this salat is supererogatory, and there shall be no congregational gathering for supererogatory prayer. Let each man among you perform salat by himself, and let him recite what Allah has taught him from His Book. And know that there is no congregation in a supererogatory prayer. So the people dispersed, and each one of them performed salat on his own, for himself.

Then when it was the night of the nineteenth of the month of Ramadan, he performed ghusl (ritual bath) when the sun had set and performed the Maghrib salat (prayer) with ghusl. After he had performed Maghrib and the four rakʿahs which he used to perform every night after Maghrib before that, he entered his house. When Bilāl gave the iqāmah for the ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم came out and led the people in salat. Then when he finished, he performed two rakʿahs while seated, as he used to perform every night, then he stood and performed one hundred rakʿahs, reciting in every rakʿah Fātiḥat al-Kitāb and Qul Huwa Allāhu Aḥad ten times. When he finished that, he performed his salat which he used to perform every night at the end of the night.

Then when it was the night of the twentieth in the month of Ramadan, he did as he had done on the previous nights in the month of Ramadan: eight rakʿahs after Maghrib and twelve rakʿahs after the ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah. Then when it was the night of the twenty-first, he performed ghusl when the sun had set and on it did the like of what he had done on the night of the nineteenth. Then when it was the night of the twenty-second, he increased in his salat, so he performed eight rakʿahs after Maghrib and twenty-two rakʿahs after the ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah. Then when it was the night of the twenty-third, he also performed ghusl just as he had performed ghusl on the night of the nineteenth and as he had performed ghusl on the night of the twenty-first, then he did the like of that.

They said: Then they asked him about the fifty prayers—what was their state in the month of Ramadan? He said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform this salat and also perform the fifty prayers as he used to perform in months other than Ramadan, and he did not reduce anything from them.

key_terms.اغْتَسَلَ: performed ghusl (ritual bath), mentioned for specific nights of Ramadan
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), including both obligatory and supererogatory forms discussed in the report
key_terms.جَمَاعَةَ: congregation in prayer, explicitly negated here for nafilah prayer
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time in which the additional nightly prayers are described
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْخَمْسِينَ: the fifty prayers, referring to the regular daily and nightly cycle of prescribed and recommended prayers
key_terms.مِائَةَ رَكْعَةٍ: one hundred rakʿahs, performed on certain nights in the narration
key_terms.نَافِلَةٌ: a supererogatory prayer, which the hadith states is not to be performed in congregation

ai.seo_question: How did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم perform the recommended prayers in the month of Ramadan, and is congregation permitted for supererogatory prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding the recommended prayers of the month of Ramadan, including additional nightly rakʿahs and special observances on the nights of the nineteenth, twenty-first, and twenty-third. It also states that supererogatory prayers are not to be held in congregation and that the regular cycle of fifty prayers was not diminished in Ramadan.
